approach: Add a remote-backed append to the athena-git RecordsWriter: fetch the remote records tip, reset the local ref to it (new `sync_from`), build the commit on that tip with optional extra parents, push with a lease, move the local ref only after the push succeeds, and retry a bounded number of times on rejection. In athena-core gh.rs add a `LandingRecords` trait with a real `GitLandingRecords` built by `GitLandingRecords::for_remote`. land_pr resolves the remote default-branch tip sha, validates every commit in remote_base..head, writes the intent before `host.merge`, and writes the landing (second parent = PR head) only after the merge is confirmed. An unconfirmed merge writes no landing and adds a PrReport warning naming the intent. Athena::land_pr builds the sink through the constructor and errors if that fails. Update the design doc and CHANGELOG.

decisions.choice: LandingRecords trait with real GitLandingRecords impl; LandPr.records is Option<&dyn LandingRecords>, None only in pre-existing tests.
decisions.reason: Existing fakes use non-hex shas that fail history.rs validation, so git-derived data stays behind the trait. New tests use a real temp repo, a bare remote and a fake host.

decisions.choice: LandingCommit.verification is derived deterministically: new fn `verification_id(job: &JobId) -> Result<RecordId, _>` in gh.rs returns the job's own RecordId (JobId::Id(r) => r.clone()); JobId::Bootstrap errors naming the commit. The doc comment and design doc state this mapping. No change to history.rs or records.rs.
decisions.reason: Verification (records.rs:718) has no id field and there is exactly one athena.verification/1 record per job, stored under the job's directory, so the job id identifies it.

rejected.option: Add an id field to Verification
rejected.why: Changes the records schema outside this job's deliverables.

decisions.choice: expected_base is a sha: land_pr fetches the remote default branch (name from PrHost::default_branch), resolves its tip sha with the existing remote_base logic, uses it as the lower bound of the commit range, and passes it to the sink's intent().
decisions.reason: LandingIntent::validate runs check_sha on expected_base (history.rs:91-104); a branch name would be refused.

rejected.option: Pass the branch name from default_branch

decisions.choice: Remote-tip build, lease push, local ref moved after push success, bounded retry; `sync_from` is a NEW reset-to-remote step (the 'distinct recover path'), not a change to an existing function.

rejected.why: A failed push leaves local ahead of remote.

decisions.choice: Extend RecordsWriter with extra parents and remote append.

decisions.reason: The client already knows it; inference is a guess.

rejected.why: Squash and one-commit rebase look alike.

decisions.choice: Unconfirmed merge: land_pr returns Ok with PrReport.warnings naming the intent id; no landing; rerun reuses an existing intent for the same PR and head.
decisions.reason: Matches the accepted reading; reconcile is job 3 part 2.

decisions.choice: Validate every commit in remote_base..head before writing the intent, in land.rs.
decisions.reason: Criterion 9; a bad PR leaves no records.

decisions.choice: Athena::land_pr calls GitLandingRecords::for_remote and returns its error rather than falling back to None.
decisions.reason: Makes the production path unable to silently skip records.

rejected.option: Fall back to records: None on constructor failure

steps: athena-git lib.rs: add Git helpers (fetch ref without moving refs, push with lease, update-ref) with tests.
records_branch.rs: factor commit build, add extra parents, new sync_from, append_to_remote with bounded retry, tests for criteria 5 and 6.
gh.rs: PrHost::merge returns MergeMethod; add PrReport.warnings.
land.rs: collect and validate commits in remote_base..head, error naming the sha.
gh.rs: add verification_id (job RecordId), LandingRecords, GitLandingRecords and for_remote; intent and landing builders that validate before writing.
land_pr: resolve remote default-branch tip sha as expected_base, write intent before merge (reuse existing for same PR and head), landing after confirmation, warning if unconfirmed.
Athena::land_pr builds the sink via for_remote and propagates its error; display.rs warning line; check drain.rs compiles.
Add records: None to old LandPr literals and update merge fakes; write tests for criteria 1-9.
Run cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked.

risks.mitigation: Update gh.rs and external_calls.rs fakes in the same step; run the full suite.

risks.risk: Records commit's second parent (PR head) missing on the remote.
risks.mitigation: The PR head is already the pushed work branch, checked by remote_head.

risks.risk: Bare-remote lease semantics differ from host branch rules.
risks.mitigation: Doc states host rules are job 4.
Reuse an existing intent for the same PR and head; tested in criterion 7.

risks.risk: Bootstrap-job commits have no verification id.
risks.mitigation: verification_id errors naming the commit sha; covered with the criterion 9 test.

demonstrations.method: Test with a real temp repo, a bare remote, a fake host and GitLandingRecords; run land_pr, then read athena/records.
demonstrations.observes: First-parent log shows the intent commit then the landing commit. Intent: PR number, head sha, head tree, expected_base equal to the remote main tip sha (asserted), job ids. Landing: PR number, head sha, host commit, merge method, commits with tree/job/verification (verification equals the job's RecordId via verification_id), intent id. Both validate.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no intent or landing writes, the records branch is missing and the test fails.

demonstrations.method: Read the parents of the landing's records commit.
demonstrations.observes: Parents are [previous records tip, PR head sha]; the intent commit has one parent.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without extra-parent support the second parent is absent and the assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Fake host whose merge returns Err; read local and remote records refs.
demonstrations.observes: Both refs hold the same tip with the intent and no landing file; land_pr returns the existing error.
demonstrations.fails_without: A landing written regardless of the merge would exist in the tree.

demonstrations.method: Fake merge reads the bare remote's records ref at call time; read again after land_pr returns.
demonstrations.observes: At merge time the remote has the intent and no landing; afterwards it has the landing.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the intent were pushed after the merge, the remote has no intent at merge time.

demonstrations.method: A hook between build and push makes another clone push a records commit; a second case moves the remote on every attempt.
demonstrations.observes: First push rejected; commit rebuilt on the fetched tip and retry succeeds; local and remote tips equal; other writer's file kept; local ref unchanged during the rejected attempt; the always-moving case ends in a bounded Contended error.
demonstrations.fails_without: A plain push without lease and rebuild fails non-fast-forward; an unbounded loop would hang.

demonstrations.method: Make a local records ref ahead of the remote, and another diverged; run the remote append and then land_pr.
demonstrations.observes: Local reset to the remote tip; write succeeds with no divergence error; leftover local commit not on the remote; next land_pr succeeds.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the reset the push is non-fast-forward or leftover commits leak.

demonstrations.method: Fake host whose merge succeeds but merged_commit stays None; run land_pr twice.
demonstrations.observes: land_pr returns Ok (the same result shape the CLI already maps today; main.rs and drain.rs exit mapping untouched in the diff); no landing record; report.warnings names the intent id; the rerun adds no second intent and no landing (counts equal).
demonstrations.fails_without: Writing a landing anyway or minting a new intent on rerun changes the counts.

demonstrations.method: Call GitLandingRecords::for_remote on a repo with a bare origin, then intent() and landing() through the returned sink; an unknown remote name errors. Wiring is shown by this test plus diff inspection that Athena::land_pr passes Some(sink) from for_remote and propagates its error (no None fallback).
demonstrations.observes: The remote athena/records holds the records written through the sink; the unknown remote gives a clear error.
demonstrations.fails_without: A sink writing only locally leaves the remote records branch empty and the test fails.

demonstrations.method: Repo where a commit between remote base and PR head lacks an Athena-Job trailer or verification; run the collection and land_pr.
demonstrations.observes: Error names that sha and says it lies between the remote base and the PR head; the records branch is unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: The commit would be skipped or land_pr would proceed to write an intent.

demonstrations.method: Run the full suite; old trailer, records/ and resync_onto_merge tests are unchanged apart from `records: None` in LandPr literals and the merge return type in fakes.
demonstrations.observes: All pass; then `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the change altered existing trailer, records/ or resync_onto_merge behavior, those unchanged tests fail; lint or format regressions fail clippy/fmt.

demonstrations.observes: The sink builds LandingIntent, Landing, LandingCommit with MergeMethod from athena_data::history, calls validate() before writing, and writes only via RecordsWriter; no new writer type.

demonstrations.method: Inspect docs/design/records-history.md, CHANGELOG.md and new doc comments.
demonstrations.observes: Design doc describes sync_from as a new reset-to-remote recover step, states the verification-id mapping, and has a failure-path table (starting state, function, cited behavior) covering rejected push, local ahead, local diverged, refused merge, unconfirmed merge and bad range commit; new functions cite design sections; CHANGELOG has an entry.
